summary:
I've been building character-creation tooling for SillyTavern (st-character-forge). Most extensions in that space generate a card in one shot from a prompt; mine runs an interview first, builds a persistent brief across turns, then produces the card, lorebook, and art without leaving the chat. I did a competitive survey of the field recently and the only real incumbent sits at 157 stars with no interview step and no lorebook authoring, which told me the niche I picked is actually open rather than crowded.

The messier week was a caching bug in the Python side of that project: a commit that marked every lore entry as "constant" (meant to help prefix-caching on the P100) quietly broke the heuristic the extension used to tell "this is the character's core description" from "this is regular lore" — suddenly everything looked equally core. Fixed it by falling back to checking the entry's title for a "— core" suffix when the source tag is missing, which turned out to matter specifically for imported cards.

I also shipped a Japanese study dashboard for myself (Keikochō), which turned into a lesson about not trusting generated audio. I tried two TTS engines for it — one silently taught the wrong pronunciation for a couple of common particles because it applies grammar rules blindly to isolated characters, the other lets me patch the specific mora before synthesizing. Now every generated clip gets checked against its expected pronunciation before it ships, and that check has already caught two real mistakes before they reached the UI.

On the infra side, I tracked down a nasty one on my home agent server: a background cron job was setting a "this is an automated session" flag globally and never clearing it, which meant that after the first daily job ran, the agent started treating every single interactive chat message as if it were unattended automation and silently refused to execute code. Took a refcounted fix so the flag only trips while a job is actually in flight.

highlights.oneLiner: Interview-first SillyTavern character-creation extension, positioned against the one 157-star incumbent
